note: One material per mesh. Team membership rides in the vertex colour channel so that one instanced draw per shape covers every owner.

backdrop.starfieldCeiling: 12% of full white over any large area; brightest eight stars reach 45% over a few dozen pixels

hull._decision: MINE. Nothing in the design states a hull palette. Chosen as a three-step near-neutral cool grey at chroma low enough (oklch C ≈ 0.014–0.018) that it cannot be mistaken for any of the four team hues, for damage red #FF3B2F, or for armed amber #FFB020.

DEEP.use: undersides, keels, shadowed structure. Sits ~4× the backdrop luminance so the hull bottom still separates from #04060A rather than merging into it.

BASE.use: the bulk of every hull. The silhouette-carrying tone at tactical zoom.

EDGE.use: upper chines and top faces. The brightest hull value; deliberately below the 45% starfield peak so a hull never out-reads a star.

OWN.use: the local player at every player count

reserved._note: echoed. The hull palette must not collide with either.

vertexColorConvention._decision: MINE. The precise convention the brief asks to be stated.
vertexColorConvention.R: team selector. 0 = take the hull palette. 255 = take the owning player's team colour. Intermediate values are a linear blend and are RESERVED — no MVP mesh emits one. A reader may treat any value outside {0,255} as a content error.
vertexColorConvention.G: hull tone index, quantised to exactly three authored values: 0 → HULL.DEEP, 128 → HULL.BASE, 255 → HULL.EDGE. No MVP mesh emits any other value. G is ignored wherever R = 255.
vertexColorConvention.shader: albedo = lerp(HULL[G], TEAM[owner], R/255). The owner colour arrives as per-instance constant data, never as a material and never as a second submesh, so one instanced draw per shape covers every owner at every player count.
vertexColorConvention.whyNotTwoMaterials: Two materials would buy a specular difference between team panel and hull plate and cost one extra draw call per shape per frame — at 5 shapes and 5 asteroid variants that is 10 extra draws for an effect invisible at 3.5 px and marginal at 79 px. Not taken.

material._note: One CMO material per mesh, identical values for every mesh. CMO's material block carries ambient/diffuse/specular/emissive/power plus eight texture slots; every texture slot is empty.
material.name: OC_Hull
material.note: diffuse is white because the albedo arrives entirely through the vertex colour channel. A reader that ignores vertex colour will render every hull white, which is the intended loud failure.

light._decision: MINE. The design states no light rig; the plates need one and it has to be stated or the plates are not reproducible.

key.note: high, front-left. Pitched steeply so the plan view at tactical zoom is lit, which is where identification happens.

fill.note: weak underside fill so a hull's keel does not go to pure backdrop at the combat view.

ambient.note: cool ambient, multiplied by albedo — never added flat, so it cannot lift the backdrop.

contrastCheck.HULL.BASE on #04060A: contrast ratio 3.9:1 — silhouette-grade, which is what it is for
contrastCheck.TEAM.OWN on HULL.BASE: the team face is always the brightest thing on a hull; it never sits adjacent to damage red because damage red is drawn over the hull bar in screen space, not on the mesh
contrastCheck.nearest collision: HULL.EDGE #828E9C against TEAM.D #A45CFF — 75° apart in hue and 0.16 apart in chroma. No hull tone is within 40° of damage red or armed amber.
